sources.title: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah): Wampanoag History
sources.note: Direct tribal history, Historical Background and modern recognition. No stale membership counts; recognition agency not inferred from the page.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Wampanoag Government Across Time
sources.note: Direct museum educational account; early seventeenth-century sachems and local councils, named female leaders.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Eel River Farm Site
sources.note: Direct archaeology page: seasonal village, quartz workshops, 37,970 artifacts and ten projects. Earliest objects do not date all village remains.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Wampanoag Pottery Sherd
sources.note: Direct object record 19PL522.1977; Early-Middle Woodland 3000-1000 BP as museum labels it. Excavation locality not specified, so not attached to Eel River.

sources.title: Aquinnah Wampanoag: Ancient Ways
sources.note: Direct sections Wetu, Epenow and Cranberry Day; historical house and escape account separated from contemporary Aquinnah festival.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Mishoon
sources.note: Indexed full museum text, modern reproduction and manufacture. No Roger Williams regional labor estimate attributed specifically to Wampanoag builders.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Playing and Learning
sources.note: Indexed full original; Wampanoag section only, distinct from English children elsewhere on the page.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: The First Thanksgiving timeline
sources.note: Direct sections 1616-1620, 1675-1676 and 1700s-late1800s. Unrelated problematic first-alphabet, Harvard foundation and Weetamoo death statements are not adopted.

sources.title: Plimoth Patuxet Museums: Wampanoag Perspectives on the Plymouth-Pokanoket Agreement
sources.note: Direct Nanepashemet interview excerpt, recorded in the 1990s; his interpretation explicitly attributed.

sources.title: Museum of the Bible: The Indian Bible, 1663
sources.note: Indexed collection record BIB.003870, Cambridge 1663. Title is not given an invented literal translation.

sources.title: Wôpanâak Language Reclamation Project: Project History
sources.note: Direct history, 1993 collaboration, written archives and related languages. Universal first-language/first-reclamation claims excluded.

sources.title: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe: WLRP August 2019 Mittark
sources.note: Direct dated community report, Mukayuhsak Weekuw translation and completed 2018-2019 school year. Plans for expansion not described as accomplished.

sources.title: Narragansett Indian Tribe: Early History
sources.note: Direct community history. Broad homeland and continuing identity used; unsupported 30,000-year archaeological assertion excluded.

sources.title: Lorén Spears: Narragansett History, Rhode Island Historical Society
sources.note: Direct named Narragansett author, seasonal living, diplomacy and 1675 attack. Does not adopt the page’s erroneous 1523 Verrazzano date, universal village population or claim that all fortified inhabitants were noncombatants.

sources.title: Rhode Island government: Purchase of Salt Pond archaeological site, 2013
sources.note: Direct 7 August 2013 state preservation announcement, site RI 110, 1100-1300 CE village and structures/storage/cooking evidence.

sources.title: Tonya Largy and E. Pierre Morenon: Maize Agriculture in Coastal Rhode Island, 2008
sources.note: NYSM Bulletin 512 chapter 6. Direct PDF fetch fails; indexed original fully exposes pp.81 and 84 using query site:exhibitions.nysm.nysed.gov/publications/bulletin/512-16671.pdf "five" "RI 110". Associated charcoal dates not called direct maize dates.

sources.title: Rhode Island Historical Society: Object Thursday, the Narragansett Basket
sources.note: Direct collection discussion, RIHS 1842.2.1, circa 1675, basswood splints, corn husk and red wool; accompanying note and workmanship.

sources.title: RIHS EnCompass: Broadside for the Sale of the Indian Reservation
sources.note: Direct fetch cache miss; indexed original accessible via site:encompass.rihs.org "Broadside" "July 11". Auction context only used; page’s 1982 federal recognition statement not adopted over tribe’s 1983 effective date.

sources.title: Narragansett Indian Tribe: Perseverance
sources.note: Direct governmental history, 1792 council, continued meetings, 1978 settlement and 11 April 1983 acknowledgment. Stale population/gathering totals and inaccurate magazine duration omitted.

sources.title: University of Rhode Island: The Narragansett Dawn collection
sources.note: Direct university collection metadata and issues list. Publication 1935-1936, not repository upload date 2006; no unsupported exact issue total.

sources.title: Lorén Spears: A Tomaquag Nikommo, 2017
sources.note: Direct contemporary Narragansett author. Opening translated greeting and later giveaway/feast account; no song words reproduced.

sources.title: Tomaquag Museum: School Days, Education in Indigenous Communities, 2018
sources.note: Direct museum article and photograph captions: Skyla Jennings learns basket making; Lorén Spears teaches a corn-husk doll workshop.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Single broad Wampanoag cultural narrative, with local examples attributed to Aquinnah, Mashpee and named mainland communities. No other nation absorbed.

geometry.assessment: Eastern Massachusetts/Cape Cod mainland polygon omits Noepe/Martha’s Vineyard and other island homelands. Public opening warns of this limitation.

batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Precontact examples foregrounded, seventeenth-century evidence identified, modern school and festival expressly later. Modern recognition is not ethnogenesis.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact Mukayuhsak Weekuw / The Children’s House from Mashpee August 2019 publication. 1663 book discussed separately without inventing translation of its title.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Continuing Narragansett nation; Niantic connections after the seventeenth-century war explained without automatically absorbing separate map records.

geometry.assessment: Broad Rhode Island ancestral-region outline; not the contemporary Charlestown reservation. Explicit public caveat.

batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 1100-1300 village, circa1675 basket, colonial policies and modern institutions separately dated. No death of the people at map endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact modern greeting and translation from Lorén Spears’s December2017 first-person museum account. No fifteenth-century alphabetic sample implied.
